arml-1998-superrelay-01.title: Vertex
arml-1998-superrelay-01.body:
Expanding, $y=x^2-20x+26$, an upward parabola whose minimum is at $x=-\frac b{2a}=10$ (the midpoint of the roots $1$ and $19$).

**Answer: 10**

arml-1998-superrelay-02.title: Constant sequence
arml-1998-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 1, $10$.)*

If all terms equal $a$: $a=\frac{a+3T}2-a$, so $2a=a+3T-2a$, $3a=3T$ and $a=T=10$.

**Answer: 10**

arml-1998-superrelay-03.title: Count
arml-1998-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 2, $10$.)*

Each row has $5$ even-numbered seats among $1,\dots,10$, and there are $10$ rows: $50$.

**Answer: 50**

arml-1998-superrelay-04.title: Rectangles and diagonals
arml-1998-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 3, $50$.)*

The value of $T$ does not matter. Since $B$ is directly above $E$, $ABEF$ and $BEDC$ are rectangles. In $ABEF$ the diagonals $AE$ and $FB$ cross at $Y$, and triangle $BYE$ is one of the four triangles they cut off, with area $\frac14[ABEF]$. Likewise triangle $BXE$ has area $\frac14[BEDC]$.

The shaded region is the union of these two triangles, so its area is $\frac14([ABEF]+[BEDC])=\frac14[ACDF]$.

**Answer: $\frac14$**

arml-1998-superrelay-05.title: Discriminant
arml-1998-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 4, $\frac14$.)*

Here $K=\frac1T=4$. Clearing denominators, $x(K-x)=K$, i.e. $x^2-Kx+K=0$. For a unique solution the discriminant $K^2-4K$ must vanish, which indeed holds for $K=4$. Then $x^2-4x+4=0$, so $x=2$.

**Answer: 2**

arml-1998-superrelay-06.title: Geometric series
arml-1998-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 5, $2$.)*

The sum is $\frac{T}{1-r}=10$, so $1-r=\frac{2}{10}$ and $r=\frac45$.

**Answer: $\frac45$**

arml-1998-superrelay-07.title: Prime factorisation
arml-1998-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 6, $\frac45$.)*

$10^4\cdot\frac45=8000=2^6\cdot5^3$, which has $(6+1)(3+1)=28$ factors.

**Answer: 28**

arml-1998-superrelay-08.title: Drop perpendiculars from $P$
arml-1998-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 7, $28$.)*

$K=4$. Let the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ to $DC$ be $E$ and to $BC$ be $F$. In the $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle $DEP$ with hypotenuse $DP=2K$: $PE=K$ and $DE=K\sqrt3$. In triangle $BFP$ (hypotenuse $2K$, angle $30^\circ$ at $B$): $PF=K$ and $BF=K\sqrt3$, so $EC=PF=K$ and $DC=DE+EC=K\sqrt3+K$.

Area $=DC^2=(K\sqrt3+K)^2=4K^2+2K^2\sqrt3$. With $K=4$: $64+32\sqrt3$, so $a+b=96$.

**Answer: 96**

arml-1998-superrelay-09.title: Eliminate
arml-1998-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 8, $96$.)*

Multiply the first equation by $T$ and subtract it from the second: $(T+1-2T)y=T+2-3T$, i.e. $(1-T)y=2-2T$, so $y=2$ (as $T\ne1$). Then $x=3-4=-1$ and $x+y=1$, independent of $T$.

**Answer: 1**

arml-1998-superrelay-10.title: Coordinates
arml-1998-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 9, $1$.)*

Put $A=(0,0)$, $C=(T,0)$. Then $D=\left(\frac{3T}2,\frac{T\sqrt3}2\right)$ and $AD^2=\frac{9T^2}4+\frac{3T^2}4=3T^2$. With $T=1$, $N=3$.

**Answer: 3**

arml-1998-superrelay-11.title: Square it
arml-1998-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 10, $3$.)*

$(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)^2=1+\sin2\theta=\frac1{T^2}=\frac19$, so $\sin2\theta=-\frac89$.

**Answer: $-\frac89$**

arml-1998-superrelay-12.title: Point-slope
arml-1998-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 11, $-\frac89$.)*

$y-16=T(x+14)$. Setting $y=0$: $x=-\frac{16}T-14=-16\cdot\left(-\frac98\right)-14=18-14=4$.

**Answer: 4**

arml-1998-superrelay-13.title: Inclusion-exclusion
arml-1998-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 12, $4$.)*

$\frac{10^4}4+\frac{10^4}5-\frac{10^4}{20}=2500+2000-500=4000$.

**Answer: 4000**

arml-1998-superrelay-14.title: Power of a point
arml-1998-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 13, $4000$.)*

$AB=16-1=15$. By power of a point, $PA\cdot PB=PC^2$: $\frac x2\left(\frac x2+15\right)=x^2$. This is $\frac{x^2}4+\frac{15x}2=x^2$, so $\frac{15x}2=\frac{3x^2}4$ and, dividing by $x>0$, $x=10$.

**Answer: 10**

arml-1998-superrelay-15.title: Complete the squares
arml-1998-superrelay-15.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 14, $10$.)*

$x^2-10x+y^2-8y=8\iff(x-5)^2+(y-4)^2=8+25+16=49$, a circle of radius $7$ centred at $(5,4)$. The largest $x$ is $5+7=12$.

**Answer: 12**
